Sometimes, your transaction just fails, but why? If you've ever deployed a contract or called a method on VeChainThor and gotten a reverted transaction, here’s how to dig into it and figure out what went wrong What Is a Reverted Transaction? A transaction reverts when: The contract throws an exception (revert, require, assert, or custom error) The gas runs out during execution The transaction violates validation rules (e.g., expired, wrong chainTag, etc.) VeChain transactions return a reverted: true flag in the receipt, but that alone doesn’t explain why it failed. How to Debug It Use the built-in debug_traceTransaction RPC method to replay a failed transaction in a simulated EVM and trace its execution. No need to deploy custom tooling — this feature is native to the Thor node when run with the appropriate flags. Step-by-Step: 1⃣ Start a local Solo Node or use your private network Run Thor with tracing enabled: thor solo --api-allow-custom-tracer --verbosity 4 2⃣ Use the debug_traceTransaction RPC method Example request: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "debug_traceTransaction", "params": ["0xYourTxHash"], "id": 1 } You’ll get back a detailed log of every opcode executed, including the point where the contract reverted. 3⃣ Look for: Stack overflows Failed require conditions Out-of-gas errors Invalid contract calls Pro Tip Most failed transactions on VeChain are due to missing VTHO (gas). Using fee delegation (via isDelegated: true) often fixes this and simplifies UX, especially for apps that require lots of transactions. Debugging failed transactions is crucial for: dApp reliability Developer sanity Optimizing gas usage Identifying logic bugs in contracts And VeChain gives you a clean, low-friction way to do it. Estas barreras han impedido que la tecnología blockchain alcance la interoperabilidad fluida que promete la Web3, limitando su adopción y creando una escasez artificial de liquidez y acceso de usuarios.
